newsitem.title: ITALY: Bankers Trust, Merrill in Italy soccer club deal.
newsitem.headline: Bankers Trust, Merrill in Italy soccer club deal.

text.p: Two U.S. banks, Bankers Trust and Merrill Lynch, joined forces with three Italian businessmen to buy Serie B soccer team Torino Calcio on Wednesday in the hope of restoring it to its former glory.

Each bank has taken a one-third stake in a company called Bullfin which has acquired an 89.93 percent interest in the soccer club from its current chairman Gian Marco Calleri for slightly more than 20 billion lire ($11.9 million).

The balance of Bullfin is owned by a company called HLS based in Genoa and owned by three businessmen -- Massimo Vidulich, who is to take over from Calleri as Torino chairman, Davide Palazzetti and Renato Bodi.

Palazzetti will be the club's managing director and Bodi, son of Luigi Bodi, who played for the club in the 1950s, will join the board of directors. Neither of the U.S. banks will be directly represented on the Torino board.
Vidulich told a news conference on Wednesday he planned to beef up the team by acquiring new players, win promotion to Serie A and float the club on the London stock exchange before the year 2000.
Torino was Italy's top club in the 1940s, winning the league championship four years in succession, but the entire team died in a plane crash in the hills outside Turin in May 1949.
The club, which since its golden age has won the league championship only once -- in 1976 -- was relegated to Serie B at the end of last season.

Vidulich also said that he and his partners intend to expand the business by developing merchandising interests and generating sales from pay-per-view television. Milan newsroom +392-66102321 ($ = 1684 Italian Lire)
